questions.question: In deductive logic, what defines a sound argument?
choices: It is valid and has all true premises
It is strong and has probable conclusions
It has true premises regardless of validity
It is an invalid argument with true premises
questions.explanation: A deductive argument is sound when it is valid and all its premises are true.

questions.question: According to Aristotle's classical linear communication model, what are the primary elements?
choices: Information source, transmitter, channel, receiver, destination, and noise
Speaker, speech, occasion, audience, and effect
Communicator, message, medium, receiver, and feedback
Sender, encoder, decoder, interpreter, and field of experience
questions.explanation: Aristotle's speaker-centred model consists of speaker, speech, occasion, audience, and effect.

questions.question: Which concept was introduced in the Shannon-Weaver model to represent something that distorts a message during transmission?
choices: Field of experience
Noise
Feedback loop
Circular interpretation
questions.explanation: The Shannon-Weaver model includes noise in the channel as a source of signal or message distortion.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four instructional quadrants of courses hosted on the SWAYAM platform?
choices: Video lecture
Specially prepared downloadable and printable reading material
Compulsory physical classroom attendance
Online discussion forum for clearing doubts
questions.explanation: The four quadrants include video lectures, reading material, self-assessment tests or quizzes, and online discussion forums.

questions.question: Under the SWAYAM digital initiative, which organization is the National Coordinator for non-technical postgraduate education?
choices: NPTEL
UGC
NCERT
AICTE
questions.explanation: The University Grants Commission (UGC) is the National Coordinator for non-technical postgraduate education on SWAYAM.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes Read-Only Memory (ROM) in a computer system?
choices: It is volatile memory that loses its contents when power is turned off
It is internal storage used exclusively for temporary CPU cache calculations
It is non-volatile memory that retains its contents when power is turned off and stores the bootstrap loader
It is an external optical storage medium used only for recording high-definition video
questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile and retains stored information when power is off; it can hold the bootstrap program used to start a computer.

questions.question: In the computer memory hierarchy, which storage component provides the fastest data access and is located directly inside the CPU?
choices: Hard Disk Drive (HDD)
Main Memory (DRAM)
Registers
Optical Disk
questions.explanation: Registers are inside the CPU and are the fastest storage units in the computer memory hierarchy.

questions.question: In statistical hypothesis testing, a Type I error occurs when a researcher:
choices: Rejects a null hypothesis that is actually true
Accepts a null hypothesis that is false
Accepts an alternative hypothesis when it is false
Fails to reject a true alternative hypothesis
questions.explanation: A Type I (alpha) error is rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true.

questions.question: The Montreal Protocol, opened for signature in 1987, was primarily established to:
choices: Control and phase out ozone-depleting substances
Mandate legally binding greenhouse gas emission reductions
Conserve world cultural and natural heritage sites
Regulate international transboundary movements of hazardous wastes
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol was established to control and phase out ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs.

questions.question: Which level of teaching, propounded by Herbart, is teacher-centred and focuses primarily on rote learning, recall, and recognition of facts?
choices: Reflective level of teaching
Memory level of teaching
Understanding level of teaching
Autonomous development level of teaching
questions.explanation: The memory level of teaching is teacher-dominated and centres on factual memorisation and recognition.
